notes: Identity is per lineage: a hunk equivalence class. Born blocks keep one id across the changes that add them. Hunk states take the first that holds of landed (a holder merged into main), inFlight (a holder open), dropped (only closed holders), obsolete (no holder and it no longer applies to main), notCarved.

edgeCases.what: two blocks share one name in one file; a spike hunk edits the second
edgeCases.design: LAYERED_DOCUMENT.md identity rules (signature first); BLOCK_DISCOVERY.md 4.1

edgeCases.what: a block inside #if/#endif; a spike hunk edits it
edgeCases.design: BLOCK_DISCOVERY.md does not say whether the guard belongs to the span

edgeCases.what: a 400-block generated file, regenerated wholesale on trunk (every block changes at once)
edgeCases.design: SCALE.md section 3, kinds before blocks (kinds@1); identity under wholesale regeneration is not designed

edgeCases.what: a file with CRLF line endings and a UTF-8 BOM
edgeCases.design: line and column semantics for CRLF and BOM are unspecified

edgeCases.what: tab indentation and non-ASCII text (columns differ from bytes and characters)
edgeCases.design: anchor column units are unspecified (BACKBONE.md 3.2)

edgeCases.what: one trunk commit prepends two lines to every source file: every line number moves, no block changes
edgeCases.design: identity by signature, anchors re-resolved by quote (BACKBONE.md 5.1)

edgeCases.what: a block the spike edits moves to another file on trunk; the hunk still applies there
edgeCases.design: SCALE.md section 4, cross-file moves through the LSH

edgeCases.what: a file the topic edits moves to a new directory before carve-outs based on it merge
edgeCases.design: git rename detection in per-path replay (SCALE.md section 4)

edgeCases.what: a file renamed by case only (fatal on case-insensitive file systems if both existed)
edgeCases.design: path identity on case-insensitive file systems is unspecified

edgeCases.what: trunk renames a block that open changes (a stack, the integration change) modify
edgeCases.design: identity carries through renames (R-ID); footprints carried to the viewed revision (R-CHG-1)

edgeCases.what: two open changes, under different topics, replace the same line differently
edgeCases.design: CHANGE_VIEWS.md section 3

edgeCases.what: a merged carve-out is reverted on trunk, then relanded by a new change
edgeCases.design: CHANGE_VIEWS.md landing coverage has no reverted state; a holder that merged is not enough

edgeCases.what: the bottom of a stack is rebased (history rewritten); the changes above still sit on its old head
edgeCases.design: a stale stack and a non-linear change history are not designed

edgeCases.what: trunk is merged into an open change: its branch now contains unrelated trunk work
edgeCases.design: footprints are relative to the merge base (CHANGE_VIEWS.md section 2), which the back-merge moves

edgeCases.what: a merge commit carries a line that is in neither parent
edgeCases.design: content attributed to no change: blame and footprints miss it

edgeCases.what: a change of binaries and sidecars only: no code block in its footprint
edgeCases.design: R-CHG-1 defines footprints as blocks only

edgeCases.what: a change opened 300 days before the window, still open, its base far behind trunk
edgeCases.design: drift (CHANGE_VIEWS.md section 3)

edgeCases.what: a tracker key only in the branch name; a title naming two keys
edgeCases.design: the topic policy (CHANGE_VIEWS.md section 2)

edgeCases.what: a carve-out merged into a feature branch, not trunk
edgeCases.design: landing is relative to a target branch

edgeCases.what: a change of landed hunks onto a release branch, rewritten
edgeCases.design: ports links (CHANGE_VIEWS.md section 2)

notModelled: two paths differing only by case in one tree
review comments replayed on a forge
